title: Sunday Pancakes
intro: Mom learned these from her own mother, who made them every Sunday before church. She still never measures anything; she just watches the batter.

ingredients.name: cannabutter
ingredients.feel: this much, about half the stick

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.feel: until it looks like this, a little more than a cup

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.instruction: In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together.
steps.sensory_cue: no lumps of baking powder left
steps.quote: I never measure the flour, just two big scoops.

steps.title: Melt the cannabutter low & slow
steps.instruction: Melt the cannabutter in a small pan on the lowest heat, then take it off the heat to cool slightly.
steps.sensory_cue: fully liquid but never bubbling or browning
steps.quote: Lowest flame. If it bubbles, you went too fast.

steps.title: Whisk the wet ingredients
steps.instruction: In another bowl, whisk the milk, egg and vanilla, then whisk in the melted butter.
steps.quote: Pour the butter in slow while you whisk so it doesn't clump.

steps.title: Combine & let the batter rest
steps.instruction: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ones and fold just until combined, then leave the batter alone for about 10 minutes.
steps.sensory_cue: a few small lumps are fine; it should fall off the spoon in a thick ribbon
steps.quote: Don't overmix. Lumps are okay. Now we let it sit.

steps.title: Cook a test pancake
steps.instruction: Heat a lightly buttered pan over medium-low. Pour in a small ladle of batter and cook until bubbles cover the top, then flip once.
steps.sensory_cue: bubbles pop and the holes stay open; edges look dry
steps.quote: The first one is always for the cook. It tells you if the pan is ready.

steps.title: Cook the rest & stack
steps.instruction: Cook the remaining batter the same way, wiping a little butter in the pan between batches, and stack the pancakes on a warm plate.
steps.sensory_cue: golden brown on both sides, springs back when pressed
steps.quote: Stack them so they stay soft. Cover with a towel.

stories.title: Sunday mornings
stories.text: My mom made these every Sunday before church. Six kids, one pan. You had to be fast or your brother got yours.

special.text: Melts the butter on the very lowest flame
special.why: Most recipes melt butter quickly; she keeps it from ever bubbling or browning.
Most recipes cook the batter right away.

follow_up_questions.question: How hot was the pan when the first pancake went in?
About how long does the butter take to melt on the lowest flame?
When you say "a little" sugar, is that closer to one spoon or two?
